predecessors.name: Principality of Chernigov
predecessors.text: Murom and Ryazan, which went with Chernigov to Sviatoslav's sons (Murom page: 1054 bequest; Oleg took Chernigov in 1094)

successors.name: Mongol Empire
successors.text: Ryazan, 'the first of all other former states of' Rus' to suffer the Mongol invasion in December 1237

successors.name: Grand Principality of Ryazan
successors.text: the same state's later Cliopatria row (Wikidata Q269109 is shared), 1453-1520

ledger.x: 1094: the Murom-Ryazan land of Chernigov's Sviatoslavichi enters the map as Ryazan.
1129: Murom-Ryazan fully splits off from Chernigov and Yaroslav's line keeps it.
1237: the Mongols take Ryazan, the first Rus' principality hit.
1238: the Mongol campaign in the Ryazan land ends.
1240: Cliopatria's Ryazan row ends and the land passes to the Mongol Empire's shape.

wars.name: Oleg's Murom campaign against Monomakh
wars.outcome: Oleg killed Monomakh's son Iziaslav at Murom in 1096 and was pushed back to Murom by Mstislav Monomakhovich; the war ended with the compromise of the Council of Liubech (19 October 1097), which left Chernigov, Tmutarakan, Ryazan and Murom to the…

wars.name: Vladimir-Suzdal's wars on Ryazan
wars.outcome: Ryazan's forces were defeated in 1177; Vsevolod III 'punished the princes of Ryazan by ousting them from their lands' in 1180 and 1187 and burned Ryazan and Belgorod in 1207; Roman I ruled Ryazan as Vsevolod's vassal (1180-1207) and died in captivity; Ryazan…

wars.name: Mongol invasion of Ryazan
wars.outcome: Ryazan fell on 21 December 1237 and its capital was destroyed; some Ryazan forces joined the Vladimir-Suzdal army against Batu near Kolomna in 1238.
